title: Positive earnings surprise on stock returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology. I will estimate abnormal returns using the market model with parameters estimated from the pre-event window [-10,-2], then calculate abnormal returns and Cumulative Abnormal Returns (CAR) for the event window [0,+2]. The key assumption is that the market model provides a reasonable counterfactual for normal returns, and that earnings surprises are exogenous conditional on firm characteristics captured by beta.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s14_data.csv")

# Define estimation and event windows
estimation_window <- c(-10, -2)
event_window <- c(0, 2)

# Function to calculate abnormal returns for each firm
calculate_abnormal_returns <- function(firm_data) {
  # Get estimation window data
  est_data <- firm_data[firm_data$event_day >= estimation_window[1] & 
                       firm_data$event_day <= estimation_window[2], ]
  
  # Estimate market model: R_it = alpha + beta * R_mt + epsilon_it
  # Note: beta is provided, so we estimate alpha
  market_model <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est_data)
  alpha_hat <- coef(market_model)[1]
  beta_hat <- coef(market_model)[2]
  
  # Calculate abnormal returns for all days
  firm_data$abnormal_ret <- firm_data$ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * firm_data$mkt_ret)
  
  return(firm_data)
}

# Calculate abnormal returns for each firm
results <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do(calculate_abnormal_returns(.)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Extract event window abnormal returns
event_data <- results[results$event_day >= event_window[1] & 
                     results$event_day <= event_window[2], ]

# Calculate CAR for each firm
car_data <- event_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_0_2 = sum(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = 'drop')

# Main results
mean_car <- mean(car_data$CAR_0_2)
se_car <- sd(car_data$CAR_0_2) / sqrt(nrow(car_data))
t_stat <- mean_car / se_car
p_value <- 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = nrow(car_data) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("=== EVENT STUDY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Event Window: [0, +2]\n")
cat("Number of firms:", nrow(car_data), "\n")
cat("Mean CAR [0,+2]:", round(mean_car, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(se_car, 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_stat, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(p_value, 4), "\n")
cat("Significant at 5% level:", ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "YES", "NO"), "\n\n")

# Daily abnormal returns
daily_ar <- event_data %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(mean_AR = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
            se_AR = sd(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
            t_stat = mean_AR / se_AR,
            .groups = 'drop')

cat("=== DAILY ABNORMAL RETURNS ===\n")
for(i in 1:nrow(daily_ar)) {
  day <- daily_ar$event_day[i]
  ar <- daily_ar$mean_AR[i]
  t_stat <- daily_ar$t_stat[i]
  cat("Day", day, ": AR =", round(ar, 4), ", t-stat =", round(t_stat, 3), "\n")
}

# Robustness check: Alternative market model using provided beta
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK (Using Provided Beta) ===\n")
robust_results <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(
    # Estimate alpha using provided beta
    est_window = ifelse(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2, 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(
    alpha_hat = mean((ret - beta * mkt_ret)[est_window == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
    abnormal_ret_robust = ret - (alpha_hat + beta * mkt_ret)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

robust_event_data <- robust_results[robust_results$event_day >= 0 & 
                                   robust_results$event_day <= 2, ]

robust_car <- robust_event_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_0_2_robust = sum(abnormal_ret_robust, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = 'drop')

mean_car_robust <- mean(robust_car$CAR_0_2_robust)
se_car_robust <- sd(robust_car$CAR_0_2_robust) / sqrt(nrow(robust_car))
t_stat_robust <- mean_car_robust / se_car_robust

cat("Robust Mean CAR [0,+2]:", round(mean_car_robust, 4), "\n")
cat("Robust t-statistic:", round(t_stat_robust, 3), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive and statistically significant CAR in the [0,+2] window, likely in the range of 2-5%. Positive earnings surprises should generate abnormal returns as the market adjusts to the better-than-expected news. The effect should be strongest on day 0 (announcement day) with some continuation into days +1 and +2 as information gets fully incorporated. The magnitude depends on how surprising the earnings were and market efficiency, but given these are confirmed positive surprises, the CAR should be economically and statistically significant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — market model; positive surprise sample; event window [0,+2]
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms with positive earnings surprises earn significantly positive CAR
